fields.h1: Build an HVAC Inspection Form for Every Service Call

fields.features_heading: What a Technician Records at Each Unit
fields.features_subheading: Describe the equipment you service and who reviews each visit. Emergent builds the form, its rules, and the database behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Checks that change with the equipment

Pick the equipment first. A gas furnace brings up burner and heat exchanger checks, while an AC or heat pump asks about the coils, the refrigerant level, and the condensate drain.
fields.feature_2:
Readings saved as numbers

Type each reading as a number, such as supply and return air temperature or motor amps. The app works out the temperature split and saves each value against the unit's serial number.
fields.feature_3:
A photo for every failed item

A failed item asks for a photo before the technician moves on. The picture of a rusted drain pan or a worn belt stays with that unit's history, ready for the next visit to compare.
fields.feature_4:
The customer signs on the tablet

The homeowner signs on the technician's tablet when the visit ends. The app emails them the report with every check, reading, and photo, and keeps the signed copy in the record.
fields.feature_5:
Safety failures go to the manager

Send each failure to the person who acts on it. A failed gas connection or heat exchanger check posts to the service manager in Slack with the address, the unit, and the photo.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can host on your servers

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and run it wherever you like. Connect the records to the dispatch or billing tool your office runs, through its API.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Reads the Inspection, and When
fields.tab_content_1:
The homeowner signs for all 16 checks

Cavendale Heating and Air sells a spring tune-up for split systems. On Linden Street, Valdemar Wynkoop works through its 16 checks, logs a 19-degree split between return and supply air, and replaces a clogged filter. The homeowner signs on his tablet at 10:42 am, and the visit joins the unit's history before he packs up.
fields.tab_content_2:
Six rooftop units each quarter, and RTU-4 fails

Every quarter, Ansgar Starkweather checks the 6 rooftop units on the Ruskwood Properties office building. This round 5 of the 6 pass. RTU-4 has a cracked, glazed drive belt, and the form flags it for repair. Property manager Hyacinth Pridmore gets an email with the unit, the failed belt, and his photo.
fields.tab_content_3:
A cracked heat exchanger reaches Slack from the basement

Rutger Emmerich opens a fall furnace check for Tallis Creek Mechanical in a basement on Alder Road. He finds a crack in the heat exchanger and marks it failed, and the form will not move on until he adds a photo. At 3:15 pm the furnace turns Unsafe, and service manager Odilia Brunell gets a Slack direct message.
fields.tab_content_4:
All 140 plan customers, with the 13 overdue on top

Pennwick Comfort Services carries 140 customers on its maintenance plan, and each one is owed a fall heating check. The register counts 96 done, 31 booked, and 13 overdue. Overdue customers sit at the top of the list, oldest due date first, and the office calls them before anyone else.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an HVAC Inspection Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up an HVAC inspection form with seasonal checks, photo-backed failures, and a signed record of every visit.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Require a photo on every fail
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the gas furnaces, heat pumps, split AC systems, and rooftop units your crews work on. Each type gets its own checks, and a technician opening a heat pump never scrolls past burner questions. Put a serial number field on every type.
fields.howto_step_2_des: ENERGY STAR advises checking the cooling system in the spring and the heating system in the fall. Build a spring cooling list and a fall heating list to match. The heating list covers gas connections, gas pressure, burner combustion, and the heat exchanger.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for each reading as a number with its unit. ENERGY STAR's checklist includes measuring voltage and current on motors, and those values belong in number fields. Numbers let the app compare this visit with the last one on the same serial number.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Make a photo required whenever a check is marked failed, with a short note beside it. A picture of a blocked condensate drain or a scorched wire answers the question later, when the customer or the property manager asks what was found.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pick who hears about each failure
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide who gets each kind of failure, and how. A failed heat exchanger might reach the service manager on Slack, while a worn belt at a rental goes to the property manager by email. Write each rule as one sentence in your prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 End the visit with a signature
fields.howto_step_6_des: Close the form with a summary of every check and a signature box for the customer. The signed visit is saved with its readings and photos in your own database, where the next technician on that unit can read it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it on one real call
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the form to Emergent and run it on one real tune-up before your whole crew uses it. Watch where the technician hesitates, then reword or reorder those checks by prompting. Add the plan register once the form holds up.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an HVAC inspection form my technicians fill out on a tablet, with checks that change for a furnace, heat pump, or AC.

faq_plan.q: What is an HVAC inspection form?
faq_plan.a: An HVAC inspection form is the record a technician fills out while checking a heating or cooling system. It marks each check pass or fail, holds readings such as air temperatures and motor current, and carries photos of problems and the customer's sign-off. The customer learns what was found, and the next technician starts from the unit's history.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an HVAC inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the equipment you service, the checks for each type, the readings to record, and who hears about a failure. Emergent writes the form and the database behind it, and you adjust either one later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What checks belong on an HVAC inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Start from ENERGY STAR's maintenance checklist. For cooling, it lists checking the refrigerant level, cleaning the evaporator and condenser coils, and inspecting the condensate drain. It also says to tighten all electrical connections and to inspect, clean, or change air filters once a month. Add your own company's items after those.

faq_plan.q: Can an HVAC inspection form fill in the customer's address and equipment?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Collect each customer's address, contact details, and equipment once. Use a customer information form for this, or start from the records you already keep. When the technician opens the job, the inspection form fills in the address and lists the units on file. The technician then adds only what changed since the last visit.

faq_plan.q: Should a residential HVAC inspection form differ from a commercial one?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in who signs and how many units one visit covers. A home visit checks one or two systems and ends with the homeowner signing. A commercial round can cover several rooftop units on one building, and the report goes to the property or facilities manager. Emergent can build both from one prompt, sharing a single equipment list.

faq_plan.q: How should failed items be handled on an HVAC inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Keep a failed unit open until someone records the repair. The technician marks the item failed and adds a photo, and the unit stays on an open list with the date it failed. When the repair is logged, it closes, and the next inspection shows the old failure beside the new readings.

faq_plan.q: Can customers sign an HVAC inspection form when they are not home?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Send the report as a link, and the customer reviews every check and signs from a phone. The app can capture an e-signature this way, saving it to the same visit record as a signature taken on the tablet. Set a reminder if the report stays unsigned for two days.

faq_plan.q: How often should a technician run an HVAC inspection form on the same unit?
faq_plan.a: Run it at least twice a year on a system that heats and cools, once ahead of each season, following the seasonal timing in ENERGY STAR's checklist. A contract may ask for more: the rooftop units in the quarterly round above get four visits a year.

faq_plan.q: Where do completed HVAC inspection forms get stored?
faq_plan.a: Every completed inspection is saved as a record in a database you own, tied to the unit's serial number and the customer. Emergent sets no response cap, and years of visits stay in one place. Connect the records to your dispatch or billing tool through its API when the office needs them there.

faq_plan.q: Can an HVAC inspection form track who is due for a maintenance plan visit?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the plan's start date and visit schedule on the customer record, and the app compares it with the last inspection on file. Customers past their due date move to the top of the register. The free tier covers building and publishing. Try the register on a single season before adding every plan.

plan.angle: The results for this query are downloadable HVAC checklists (PDF, Excel, Etsy listings) and field-service vendors' template pages. None shows the form working on a call: a technician picking the equipment type, typing readings, photographing a failed part, the customer signing, and a manager seeing which maintenance plan customers are overdue. This page shows a working HVAC inspection form at four moments (a residential spring tune-up, a quarterly rooftop unit round, a failed furnace safety check, the maintenance plan register), every inspection saved to a database the company owns. Check items are quoted from ENERGY STAR's maintenance checklist; no code, safety or efficiency claims.
